notablePrerequisites: This combo has a chance of failure based on the amount of starting mana you have and your first few coin flips. It may take significantly more or less mana than the amount shown. See the widget below for calculations.
description:
Cast the instant or sorcery that creates a copy of a creature by paying its mana cost, targeting Sakashima of a Thousand Faces.
When you cast that spell, Krark, any additional copies of Krark, and Storm-Kiln Artist trigger.
Resolve the Storm-Kiln Artist trigger, creating a Treasure token.
Resolve all Krark triggers, copying that spell for each flip you won, and returning the original to your hand as long as you lost at least one flip.
Each time you copy a spell, Storm-Kiln Artist triggers, creating a Treasure token.
Resolve each copy of that spell, creating a token copy of Krark each time.
Activate all your Treasure tokens by tapping and sacrificing them, adding one mana of any color for each one.
If that spell is back in your hand, repeat from step 1.
If you won every flip, instead resolve the card itself, creating one more Krark token and putting the card into your graveyard.
If you manage to pass a critical threshold of Krark copies before the copying spell ends up in your graveyard, this combo is overwhelmingly likely to be an infinite loop from that point on. See the widget below for failure chances.
Once you have infinite mana and infinite copies of Krark, you can repeat this loop with any instant or sorcery you can cast.
